land.text: the Czech Republic, one of the two 'constituent states' of Czechoslovakia; the territory 'was divided along the existing internal borders'

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Czechoslovakia row ends 1991 while its Czech Republic row starts 1992, so 1992 has no Czechoslovak shape; the state itself lasted to 31 December 1992.

correction.text: Shape unchanged (80,272 km2); it holds from 1 January 1993, not 1992: 'On 31 December 1992, Czechoslovakia was peacefully dissolved' and the infobox gives 'Czech Republic: 1 January 1993'

keyframe_review.note: Years only: Cliopatria starts the row in 1992, the pages date the state from 1 January 1993. Area 80,272 km2 against the infobox 78,871 km2 (ratio 1.018). The 1992 year belongs to Czechoslovakia (dissolution took effect on 31 December 1992), whose Cliopatria row ends in 1991.

Same outline as 1992 (80,272 km2). The 1996 treaty on the common border and the 1997 awards of the Sance area to Slovakia and the Sidonie area to the Czech Republic move less than a grid cell, and the pages give no coordinates or areas, so the shape is unchanged.
Same outline (80,272 km2); the page records no frontier change to 2024.

ledger.note: 1993-01-01: the Czech Republic becomes an independent state. 'On 31 December 1992, Czechoslovakia was peacefully dissolved, with its constituent states becoming the independent states of the Czech Republic and Slovakia'; infobox 'Czech Republic: 1 January 1993'. The Federal Assembly's Constitution Act 542 of 25 November 1992 agreed the split (Dissolution of Czechoslovakia page).

certainty.note: The border with Slovakia follows the former internal boundary, settled 'via mutual negotiations, financial compensation' and then 'an international treaty covering the border modifications' (Dissolution of Czechoslovakia page) (1996 treaty; Sance to Slovakia and Sidonie to the Czech Republic in 1997); the borders with Germany, Austria and Poland are inherited.

sources.title: Czech Republic

sources.title: Dissolution of Czechoslovakia
sources.note: Act 542 of 25 November 1992, effect 31 December 1992, division along the internal borders, the Sance and Sidonie awards of 1997, the 1996 border treaty.

notes: Cliopatria's Czech Republic row (1992..2024) starts a year before the state; the dossier starts on 1 January 1993 and the czech-republic_1992 verdict moves the shape to 1993. Czechoslovakia's Cliopatria row ends 1991, so the Czechoslovakia dossier (eu-21) should carry its last shape through 31 December 1992. The Sance (to Slovakia) and Sidonie (to the Czech Republic) awards of 1997 are named on the Dissolution page without coordinates or areas and are below the grid's resolution; they are left out of the ledger rather than placed from memory. Slovakia (Wikidata Q33946, shared with Czechoslovakia) is another part's dossier. The English short name Czechia was recommended later and 'directed' by the Czech government in 2016 (Czech Republic page); the dossier keeps the Cliopatria name.
